name: Sheshbazzar
title: Prince of Judah and Temple Rebuilder
summary: Sheshbazzar was a prince of Judah appointed by the Persian king Cyrus to lead the first group of Jewish exiles back to Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. He was entrusted with returning the temple vessels that Nebuchadnezzar had plundered and laid the foundation for the new temple in Jerusalem. His role marked the beginning of the rebuilding of the Jewish community in their homeland.

keyEvents.title: Cyrus hands over the temple vessels to Sheshbazzar
keyEvents.description: The Persian king Cyrus ordered that the gold and silver vessels taken by Nebuchadnezzar from the temple in Jerusalem be handed over to Sheshbazzar, prince of Judah, to be brought back.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as Governor
keyEvents.description: Sheshbazzar was appointed by Cyrus as governor (tirsata/pechah) over the province of Judah, with a mandate to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Return of the Temple Vessels to Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Sheshbazzar led the transport of the sacred vessels from Babylon back to Jerusalem, symbolizing the restoration of Jewish worship.

keyEvents.title: The foundation of the new temple is laid
keyEvents.description: Sheshbazzar laid the foundation of God's house in Jerusalem, thus starting the great rebuilding project that was later completed under Zerubbabel.

keyEvents.title: Report to King Darius about the construction work
keyEvents.description: When opponents tried to stop the temple building, a letter to King Darius referred to Sheshbazzar's original work on the foundation as proof that the construction project had been legally authorized by Cyrus.
